title: Halting simulation on a delimited word
statement: Let $z,x$ be Boolean words, and let $l$ be a Boolean word. Suppose $z=\mathrm{pre}\,\mathrm{dbl}(l)\,(0,1)\,x$, where $\mathrm{pre}$ is a Boolean word, and let $s$ satisfy the invariant that its work-head index is at most the length of its computed-value list, every marked index is smaller than that length, its phase is a main phase, and a phase outside the walking phases has work-head index zero. For any $B\in\mathbb N$ with $|s.\mathrm{vals}|+|l|\le B$, the circuit-evaluation machine, started in the configuration encoding $s$ at the input position immediately after $\mathrm{pre}$, halts with output equal to the Boolean value obtained by recursively processing $l$ from $s$, within $(|l|+1)(2B+4)$ steps. This holds for either setting of the exactness parameter.
hypotheses_covered: the start index $|\mathrm{pre}|$ is at most $|z|$
$s$ satisfies all four conjuncts of the invariant
caveat: The informal definitions supplied do not include the recursive evaluator or the configuration encoding used in the statement; these are described by their roles.
